specs.family: Ollama (OpenAI-compatible + native API). Note: the user's trigger message also asked about a "Clive" CLI — researched and reported under `sources` (first entry) since it turned out to be a client, not a model-hosting family, so it doesn't fit this schema's per-family fields.
specs.install_and_start:
Windows/macOS/Linux: download the installer from https://ollama.com/download (Windows: OllamaSetup.exe, no admin rights required). First run: launch the app, optionally sign in for Ollama Cloud models or skip and stay fully local. Pull a model with `ollama pull <name>` (e.g. `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b`) or just `ollama run <name>` which pulls-then-chats; verify with an interactive session, exit via `/bye`. Server listens on http://127.0.0.1:11434 by default (change with OLLAMA_HOST).

Windows specifics (docs.ollama.com/windows): Ollama installs as a native Windows **application with a system-tray/login item**, not a Windows Service — if the user quits the tray icon, or it never launched, nothing listens on port 11434 and Runesmith will see connection-refused. A real background service (survives logoff/reboot without a UI session) requires manually wrapping it with a tool like NSSM using the separate ollama-windows-amd64.zip; that is not the default install path. Logs: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Ollama\server.log (and app.log, upgrade.log); models default to %HOMEPATH%\.ollama\models (overridable via OLLAMA_MODELS, set via Windows "Edit environment variables for your account", then restart the tray app). Linux: `ollama serve` if not auto-started; systemd logs via `journalctl -u ollama`. macOS logs: ~/.ollama/logs/server.log.

Model-not-pulled friction: omitting a tag resolves to `:latest`, which can silently be a different size/quantization than expected — always pull/reference an explicit tag (Runesmith's PRESETS already do this, e.g. "qwen2.5-coder:7b").
specs.endpoints:
Local, unauthenticated by default — Ollama ignores any Authorization/API-key header on the local server (auth only matters for the Cloud variant below).

OpenAI-compatible surface (base http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1, matches Runesmith's "ollama" PRESET base_url):
- POST /v1/chat/completions — supported request fields per docs.ollama.com/api/openai-compatibility: model, messages, temperature, top_p, max_tokens, stop, stream, seed, response_format, tools, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, reasoning_effort. NOT supported (silently ignored): tool_choice, logit_bias, user, n, logprobs, and — critically — anything context-related (see context_window). max_tokens maps through to Ollama's native output-length option.
- POST /v1/completions — prompt-based, same JSON-mode support, no best_of/echo/logit_bias/user/n.
- GET /v1/embeddings, GET /v1/models and /v1/models/{model} — standard OpenAI-shaped {"object":"list","data":[{"id":...}]}. This is what Runesmith's `providers.list_models()` hits for kind="openai".
- POST /v1/responses — non-stateful only (no previous_response_id/conversation).
- Cloud: set OLLAMA_API_KEY and point base_url at https://ollama.com/v1 instead of localhost — a completely different, hosted deployment; not what Runesmith's local "ollama" preset uses.

Native API (http://127.0.0.1:11434, no /v1):
- POST /api/generate and POST /api/chat — model (required), messages/prompt, format (see structured_output), options.num_ctx (works here, NOT on /v1), keep_alive (default "5m", works here, NOT reliably on /v1), stream (defaults true on native, unlike OpenAI's stream=false default — Runesmith never touches native endpoints so this doesn't affect it directly).
- GET /api/tags — lists locally pulled models, {"models":[{"name": "...", ...}]}. This is exactly what Runesmith's `discover_local()` polls at http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags (providers.py:89) — confirmed correct against current docs.
- POST /api/show — model detail (Modelfile, template, parameters incl. any baked-in num_ctx, system prompt).
- POST /api/pull — downloads a model; streams NDJSON progress by default, or set stream:false for one final object. 404 with {"error":"model 'x' not found, try pulling it first"} is what you get from /api/chat or /api/generate (and the OpenAI-compat layer) when the model was never pulled — see errors.
specs.structured_output:
Native /api/chat and /api/generate: a `format` field accepts either the string "json" (loose "produce valid JSON" mode) or a full JSON Schema object, which since Ollama v0.5 is compiled into a grammar (via llama.cpp) that constrains generation to match the schema exactly (docs.ollama.com/capabilities/structured-outputs; ollama.com/blog/structured-outputs).

OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions: response_format {"type":"json_object"} is translated to native format:"json" (loose, not schema-constrained). response_format {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":...,"schema":{...}}} — matching OpenAI's own newer shape — is extracted and passed through to the native schema-grammar path in current source (openai package's ChatCompletionRequest.ResponseFormat.JsonSchema, per github.com/ollama/ollama source as of Sept 2026). This exactly matches how Runesmith's OpenAICompatInstrument builds its request body (instruments.py:287-291, json_mode="json_schema" or "json_object"). CAVEAT — version-dependent: GitHub issue ollama/ollama#10001 ("Improve compatibility with OpenAI structured outputs json_schema response_format") reported this being silently ignored in earlier builds; it's closed but I could not confirm an exact fixed-in version from docs alone, so verify against the actually-installed Ollama build rather than assuming. Ollama Cloud models do not support structured outputs at all (docs.ollama.com/capabilities/structured-outputs). Ollama's own docs also recommend also embedding the schema as text in the prompt and using temperature 0 for reliability — Runesmith's OpenAICompatInstrument already does the former (instruments.py:282-283, appends the schema into the system instruction) regardless of json_mode, which is a good match to documented best practice.
specs.context_window:
Two official pages currently disagree, and the discrepancy is itself the finding: docs.ollama.com/faq states a flat "default context window size of 4096 tokens." docs.ollama.com/context-length (a newer 2026-era page, alongside a VRAM-based auto-scaling feature described in ~v0.32.x-era secondary sources) states scaled defaults: <24 GiB VRAM → 4k context, 24–48 GiB → 32k, ≥48 GiB → 256k. For "modest machines" (Runesmith's target audience — no GPU, or a small one) this converges on the same practical number: 4,096 tokens by default, either way.

Ways to raise it: (1) server-wide via OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=<n> environment variable before starting Ollama (e.g. `OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=32000 ollama serve` on Linux, or set as a Windows user environment variable then restart the tray app); (2) per-model, baked in via a Modelfile with `PARAMETER num_ctx <n>` then `ollama create <name> -f Modelfile`; (3) per-request via options.num_ctx — but **only on the native /api/generate and /api/chat endpoints**. The OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions endpoint that Runesmith's OpenAICompatInstrument exclusively uses has no field for this: extra/unknown JSON is dropped by the fixed request struct, confirmed by github.com/ollama/ollama PR #11249 ("expose Ollama native parameters (think, keep_alive) through OpenAI API") which is still open/unmerged as of today and explicitly does not yet cover num_ctx either, plus community reports (e.g. issue threads referencing "#11409") that num_ctx nested under "options" or sent top-level on /v1 is silently ignored on current builds.

Silent truncation: when input+expected-output exceeds the active context window, Ollama does NOT error — it drops tokens from the FRONT of the prompt (so system instructions/schema text, which Runesmith puts first, are what disappears) and generates from whatever remains, returning a normal-looking 200 response. This is only visible in Ollama's own server log ("truncating input prompt"), never in the HTTP response Runesmith parses. Given Runesmith's prompts run 9,000–15,000 input tokens plus up to 8,000 answer tokens, this will trigger on virtually any default Ollama install unless the operator has separately created a bigger-context model or raised OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH.

One more wrinkle: a model's library page (e.g. ollama.com/library/qwen2.5-coder) advertises a "32K context window" — that is the model architecture's maximum, not the context Ollama actually allocates at runtime, which is governed purely by the settings above.

errors.situation: Ollama app/service is not running (Windows tray icon closed or never launched; Linux `ollama serve` not started)
errors.plain_words: Ollama isn't running. On Windows look for the llama icon in the system tray or launch "Ollama" from the Start menu; on Linux/macOS run `ollama serve`. Nothing is listening on port 11434 yet.
errors.http_status: none — connection refused before any HTTP response
errors.body_example: e.g. [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it / ConnectionRefusedError

errors.situation: Model name was never pulled locally, or the tag is wrong (omitted tag resolves to :latest)
errors.plain_words: This model hasn't been downloaded onto this computer yet. Run `ollama pull <model>` with the exact name (check `ollama list` for what's actually installed), or fix a typo'd/omitted tag.
errors.source: docs.ollama.com/api/errors; multiple ollama/ollama GitHub issues (#1254, #2203, #311 on OpenHands)
errors.body_example: {"error":"model 'qwen2.5-coder:7b' not found, try pulling it first"}

errors.situation: Malformed request body or invalid JSON schema
errors.plain_words: The request Runesmith sent wasn't valid for this server — check the JSON schema is plain JSON Schema with no vendor extensions, and that fields like max_tokens are positive integers.
errors.body_example: {"error":"descriptive message"}

errors.situation: Prompt + expected answer exceeds the active context window (very likely given Runesmith's 9,000-15,000 input tokens against Ollama's ~4k default, and no way to raise it from the /v1 endpoint Runesmith uses)
errors.plain_words: There is no error here — that's the danger. Ollama quietly drops the earliest part of the prompt (including system instructions) to fit its context window and answers from what's left; the reply will look confused, ignore instructions, or fail schema checks for no obvious reason. Fix: create a custom model with a bigger context (Modelfile + `PARAMETER num_ctx 20000`, then `ollama create`), or set OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH before starting Ollama — nothing in a single /v1 request can fix this.
errors.source: docs.ollama.com/context-length; github.com/ollama/ollama PR #11249 discussion; community reports (RepoFold, Shylin26/kepler issue #16)
errors.body_example: n/a — a normal-looking completion, just missing content the model never saw

errors.situation: Model was idle for more than keep_alive (default 5 minutes) and got unloaded from memory
errors.plain_words: If Runesmith waits more than five minutes between calls to the same local model, the next call will be slow again while Ollama reloads it — this is expected, not a bug. There's currently no way to extend this from the endpoint Runesmith uses (keep_alive is native-API-only, and even natively must be resent every call).
errors.http_status: n/a (just added latency, not an error)
errors.body_example: n/a

errors.situation: response_format json_schema silently ignored or malformed structured output on an older/unpatched Ollama build
errors.plain_words: If JSON replies come back as prose or malformed despite response_format, the installed Ollama build may predate full json_schema support on /v1. Upgrade Ollama, or rely on response_format json_object plus the schema embedded in the prompt text (which Runesmith already does).
errors.source: github.com/ollama/ollama issue #10001 (closed, fix version unconfirmed from docs alone — version-dependent)
errors.body_example: n/a — malformed/prose content in the message field

errors.situation: Rate limiting or gateway failure — only relevant if pointed at Ollama Cloud (ollama.com/v1) rather than the local 127.0.0.1 preset
errors.plain_words: This only applies if the user configured the hosted Ollama Cloud endpoint with an API key, not the default local install. A rate limit or an unreachable cloud model surfaces as these codes.

errors.situation: Model fails mid-generation (crash, OOM) after streaming has already started
errors.plain_words: The server already sent a 200 and started streaming, then failed partway through — the failure shows up as an error object inside the stream, not as a changed HTTP status.
errors.http_status: 200 followed by an in-stream error object
errors.body_example: {"error":"an error was encountered while running the model"}

runesmith_gaps: runesmith/instruments.py:264-321 (OpenAICompatInstrument.complete) never sends any context-length hint and can only reach Ollama through /v1/chat/completions, which silently drops num_ctx however it's sent (top-level or nested) — confirmed unsupported by docs.ollama.com/context-length and by the still-open, unmerged github.com/ollama/ollama PR #11249. Runesmith's own prompts run 9,000-15,000 input tokens plus up to 8,000 answer tokens, far beyond Ollama's ~4k default context on any machine under 24 GiB VRAM — every Ollama call risks silent front-truncation of the system prompt/schema block, with success (HTTP 200) and no signal in the receipt that anything was cut.

runesmith/app/providers.py:19-23 (PRESETS 'ollama' entry) — the blurb/setup string ('ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b') says nothing about the context-window problem above and does not set up a bigger-context model or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH, so a non-technical user following it exactly, out of the box, will hit silent truncation on any of Runesmith's real prompts.

runesmith/instruments.py:44-51 (classify()) has no rule for Ollama's 'model ... not found, try pulling it first' 404 — '404' is absent from TRANSPORT_MARKERS (only 429/502/503/504 are listed) and OUTPUT_MARKERS doesn't match the phrase either, so it falls through to the documented default ('unknown errors are transport'). Router.call() (instruments.py:370-388) then burns the full ~9-minute DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S ladder (15+30+45+60+90+120+180s) retrying what is really a permanent configuration error (typo'd or un-pulled model name) before finally raising TransportCensored, instead of failing fast with a clear 'pull this model first' message.

runesmith/instruments.py:264-321 (OpenAICompatInstrument) also has no way to set keep_alive, since that field is native-API-only per current Ollama and the open PR #11249 that would expose it through /v1 is unmerged — after any 5+ minute gap between calls (Ollama's default keep_alive) the next call silently pays a full model-reload latency with nothing in the CallOutcome/receipt to explain why that one call was unusually slow.

runesmith/app/providers.py:86-99 (discover_local) correctly polls http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags (matches current docs exactly) with a 0.8s timeout, but neither providers.py nor instruments.py has any plain-language copy for the very common 'Ollama app isn't running yet' case beyond a bare connection-refused surfacing as a generic transport error — worth noting since Windows Ollama is a tray application, not a background service (docs.ollama.com/windows), so a message like 'look for the llama icon in your system tray, or open Ollama from the Start menu' would materially help the non-technical audience this is built for.

specs.versions_covered: Ollama documentation as published at docs.ollama.com and github.com/ollama/ollama (main branch), retrieved 2026-09-27. docs.ollama.com pages are not individually version-stamped; secondary sources place the current stable line around v0.32-v0.34 (2026). Several behaviors are explicitly version-dependent and were flagged as such above rather than stated flatly: (1) the flat-4096 vs VRAM-scaled context-window default (two current official pages disagree — likely reflects a 2026 feature rollout not yet reconciled across docs); (2) whether response_format json_schema on /v1/chat/completions is fully honored (issue #10001, closed, exact fix version not confirmed from docs); (3) num_ctx/keep_alive exposure on /v1/chat/completions (confirmed NOT available as of today via an open, unmerged PR #11249, but this is an active area — reconfirm before relying on it staying unavailable). Recommend verifying all three against `ollama --version` and `ollama show <model>` on the actual machine used for stand-ins.

specs.family: LM Studio (local desktop app + bundled `lms` CLI + local OpenAI-compatible server), lmstudio.ai
specs.versions_covered: Current released app as of 2026-09-27 is v0.4.25 (Sep 19, 2026), per the official changelog (https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio). The default-context-length behavior described below dates from v0.4.16 (Jun 8, 2026). Individual docs pages on lmstudio.ai/docs (mirrored at github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs) are not version-stamped; lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt's own header reads "LM Studio 0.4.1 [lm-studio-041]", which does not match the current app version 0.4.25 — that string looks like a docs-bundle tag, not the app release, so treat it as "current as crawled," not pinned to one build.
specs.install_and_start:
Download page: https://lmstudio.ai/download (Windows, macOS, Linux). Windows: run the downloaded `LM-Studio-Setup-*.exe`; installer handles everything. macOS: open the `.dmg`, drag to Applications; pick the Apple Silicon build on M1–M5 Macs for Metal acceleration, Intel build otherwise. Linux: download the `.AppImage`, `chmod +x` it, and run — no system install, portable app. (Sources: https://www.promptquorum.com/local-llms/how-to-install-lm-studio , https://lmsa.app/blog/how-to-install-lm-studio-on-windows-mac-and-linux-a-beginners-guide/ — these are third-party guides, not lmstudio.ai itself, but match lmstudio.ai/download's own OS list.)

First model: open the app, go to the "Discover" tab, pick a curated model or search (e.g. "Llama"), download it. (https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt)

Starting the server (NOT automatic — this is the key out-of-the-box gotcha): either (a) GUI — open the "Developer" tab and toggle "Start Server" on, or (b) CLI — `lms server start` (add `--port 1234` to be explicit; 1234 is the default). `lms` ships inside the LM Studio install; you must have opened the app at least once before `lms` works, and `lms --help` verifies it. (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/cli , https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/core/server , https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/1_developer/0_core/0_server/index.md)

Because the server must be started by hand every time (no persistent background service the way Ollama typically runs), a non-technical user who just installs LM Studio and leaves the app closed, or forgets to flip the Developer-tab switch, will see nothing on port 1234 at all — a plain connection-refused, not an LM Studio error message.
specs.endpoints:
Base URL: `http://localhost:1234/v1` (port 1234 is the default shown throughout LM Studio's own docs and quickstarts, e.g. `lms server start --port 1234`; changeable in Developer tab or via `--port`). Sources: https://lmstudio.ai/llms-full.txt , https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat

Auth: none by default — "By default, LM Studio does not require authentication for API requests." An optional bearer-token toggle exists in Developer → Server Settings; when enabled, every REST/SDK call needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs — 1_developer/0_core/authentication.mdx, fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com)

OpenAI-compatible endpoints (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat and its subpages):
- `GET /v1/models` — "Returns the models visible to the server. The list may include all downloaded models when Just-In-Time loading is enabled." (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat/models) Standard OpenAI-style `{"data":[{"id": "...", ...}]}` shape is implied by "OpenAI-compatible" framing and by model ids following a `publisher/model` pattern (e.g. `qwen/qwen3-4b-2507`, `openai/gpt-oss-20b`); newer builds add a per-model `capabilities` array. I could not pull a verbatim example JSON body from the docs site (the fetched pages describe the endpoint but don't render the sample payload) — treat the exact field list as likely-correct-but-not-independently-confirmed-verbatim today.
- `POST /v1/chat/completions` — documented request fields: `model`, `messages`, `temperature`, `top_p`, `top_k`, `max_tokens`, `stream`, `stop`, `presence_penalty`, `frequency_penalty`, `logit_bias`, `repeat_penalty`, `seed`, plus `response_format` (documented separately, see structured_output). Chat template is applied automatically for chat-tuned models. (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/developer/openai-compat/chat-completions)
- `POST /v1/completions`, `POST /v1/embeddings`, `POST /v1/responses` also exist; an Anthropic-compatible `/v1/messages` was added around v0.4.22. (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/tree/main/1_developer/3_openai-compat , https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio)

Response shape for chat completions follows the OpenAI convention Runesmith already assumes (`choices[0].message.content` string, `finish_reason` including `"length"` on truncation, a `usage` object with `prompt_tokens`/`completion_tokens`) — this is asserted by LM Studio's "OpenAI-compatible" framing and by third-party client libraries (e.g. liteLLM's LM Studio provider) rather than a verbatim doc example I could reproduce.
specs.context_window:
Context length is a **model-load-time setting**, not a per-request field in `/v1/chat/completions` — there is no way for an API caller to raise it on a single call; it's whatever the model was (JIT-)loaded with.

App-wide default: LM Studio v0.4.16 (Jun 8, 2026) shipped "Updated default context length to 8k tokens" (https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio-v0.4.16 ; corroborated by https://lmstudio.ai/changelog/lmstudio listing this as a v0.4.16 Build 2 change). Before that change, multiple independent community sources reported LM Studio defaulting new/JIT loads to 2,048–4,096 tokens regardless of the model's trained maximum (https://fast.io/resources/lm-studio-context-length/ , a Zed editor bug report about LM Studio ignoring configured context and using its own default: https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/33938). Given Runesmith's stated request sizes (9,000–15,000 prompt tokens + up to 3,000–8,000 answer tokens, i.e. up to roughly 23,000 tokens total), **even the current 8k default is too small out of the box** — every real Runesmith call would overflow it.

Raising it: per-model defaults are set in the app's "My Models" tab → gear icon → Context Length (also GPU offload, Flash Attention) — these apply whenever that model loads, including via JIT (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/app/advanced/per-model). Also settable from the Chat tab's right-hand preset sidebar, or from the CLI with `lms load <model> --context-length=<N>` (https://lmstudio.ai/docs/cli/local-models/load).

On overflow, current versions do not silently truncate — they return/log an explicit refusal. Verbatim text from a live LM Studio instance (via a GitHub bug report, not official docs): *"Trying to keep the first 111490 tokens when context the overflows. However, the model is loaded with context length of only 32768 tokens, which is not enough. Try to load the model with a larger context length, or provide a shorter input."* (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker/issues/546). This is real observed server behavior, not a documented API contract, so the exact wording/HTTP status is not guaranteed stable across versions. A related open bug describes context overflow being handled ungracefully after a large tool response (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker/issues/1806), and on Apple Silicon MLX models a separate "context auto-fit" feature can override the user's configured context length based on available RAM (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/lmstudio-bug-tracker/issues/2250) — both are open/unresolved as of the changelogs reviewed, so treat overflow behavior as hardware- and version-dependent, not a single guaranteed error shape.

Just-In-Time (JIT) loading: a chat-completions call against a model that isn't currently loaded triggers LM Studio to load it automatically (no need to `lms load` first), using that model's per-model default context length (or the app default of 8k if none was set). Auto-Evict is on by default and keeps at most one JIT-loaded model in memory at a time; idle models are unloaded after a default 60-minute TTL, overridable app-wide, per-request (`"ttl": <seconds>` in the payload), or via `lms load <model> --ttl <seconds>`. (https://github.com/lmstudio-ai/docs/blob/main/1_developer/0_core/ttl-and-auto-evict.md, fetched raw)

errors.situation: LM Studio app is installed but the local server was never started (Developer-tab toggle off, or `lms server start` never run) — the default out-of-the-box state right after install+download.

In LM Studio, open My Models, click the gear icon next to the model, and raise its Context Length (try 16,384 or 32,768) before using it with Runesmith — the default of 8,000 tokens is too small for Runesmith's requests.

specs.install_and_start:
llama-server (github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md):
- Build from source: `cmake -B build && cmake --build build --config Release -t llama-server` → binary at ./build/bin/llama-server.
- Docker: `docker run -p 8080:8080 -v /path/to/models:/models ghcr.io/ggml-org/llama.cpp:server -m models/7B/ggml-model.gguf -c 512 --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080`.
- Quick start: `./llama-server -m models/7B/ggml-model.gguf -c 2048`.
- Default listen address: 127.0.0.1:8080 (matches providers.py's "llamacpp" preset base_url http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1).
- Latest release as of today: tag b11222, published 2026-09-27 (github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/releases). A recent (2026 H2) addition is "router mode": start `llama-server` with no `-m`, add `--models-dir PATH` (+ optional `--models-preset config.ini`, `--models-max N` [default 4], `--no-models-autoload`) and it auto-discovers GGUF files and loads them on first request instead of requiring one model per process (huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/model-management-in-llamacpp, dated 2025-12-11; medium.com/@kalyanks/the-new-router-mode-in-llama-cpp-server-27f4e3606be9).

KoboldCpp (github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp):
- Windows/macOS/Linux prebuilt executables from github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/releases/latest (no separate install step — just run the binary, e.g. `koboldcpp.exe`).
- From source: `python koboldcpp.py [model.gguf] [port]`.
- Default port: 5001 (http://localhost:5001), configurable with `--port`. Sources: lite.koboldai.net/koboldcpp_api, raw README at raw.githubusercontent.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/concedo/README.md.
- Current release line observed on SourceForge mirror: v1.90.2 (sourceforge.net/projects/koboldcpp/files/v1.90.2/) — treat as approximate/version-dependent, not the canonical release page.
specs.endpoints:
llama-server:
- POST /v1/chat/completions — body fields documented include model, messages, temperature/top_p/top_k, n_predict (aliased by max_tokens for OpenAI compat — max_tokens is honored, max_completion_tokens reportedly is not, per community reports on github.com/abetlen/llama-cpp-python/issues/1907 and github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/8634), stream, stop, response_format, reasoning_effort, reasoning_format, chat_template_kwargs, parallel_tool_calls, plus multimodal content types. Response has choices[0].message.content, finish_reason, usage.{prompt_tokens,completion_tokens,total_tokens}, and a llama.cpp-specific timings block. (github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md)
- GET /v1/models — OpenAI-shaped: {"object":"list","data":[{"id":"<path-or---alias>","object":"model","created":...,"owned_by":"llamacpp","meta":{...}}]}. Confirmed verbatim from the README. This matches exactly what providers.py's discover_local()/list_models() expect (`body["data"][i]["id"]`) — no gap here in normal (single-model) mode.
- In router mode there is also a separate GET /models (no /v1 prefix) that lists all discovered models with a status of loaded/loading/unloaded (huggingface.co/blog/ggml-org/model-management-in-llamacpp); I could not get the exact JSON shape for this specific non-/v1 endpoint from official docs — treat as uncertain/version-dependent. Runesmith's code only ever calls the /v1/models path, so this doesn't affect it.
- GET /health — 200 {"status":"ok"} when ready; 503 {"error":{"code":503,"message":"Loading model","type":"unavailable_error"}} while loading (README, verbatim).
- No API key required by default (optional `--api-key`), matches PRESETS['llamacpp']['key']=='none'.

KoboldCpp:
- POST /v1/chat/completions and GET /v1/models, both under the /v1 route (e.g. http://localhost:5001/v1/chat/completions). Full endpoint list published at /api (Swagger) and https://lite.koboldai.net/koboldcpp_api. KoboldCpp accepts extra non-OpenAI sampler fields (min_p, dry_multiplier, etc.) as extensions on top of the OpenAI body — harmless for Runesmith since it never sends them.
- I could not get a verbatim example of KoboldCpp's GET /v1/models JSON to confirm it uses the same {"data":[{"id":...}]} wrapper as llama.cpp/OpenAI — treat this as unverified/needs a live check when you have KoboldCpp running, since Runesmith's discover_local()/list_models() code assumes that exact shape for any "openai"-kind preset.
specs.structured_output:
llama-server:
- `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` — free-form JSON, supported.
- `response_format: {"type":"json_schema", ...}` — schema-constrained JSON via internal conversion to a GBNF grammar. The README's own inline example shows a flat shape (`{"type":"json_schema","schema":{...}}`), quoted verbatim from raw.githubusercontent.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/master/tools/server/README.md. However, PR #12168 ("server: fix response_format w/ json_schema.schema", merged 2025-03-04, github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/12168) explicitly fixed a regression in "response_format.json_schema.schema handling" — i.e. the **nested OpenAI-standard shape** `{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":...,"schema":{...}}}` (which is exactly what Runesmith's OpenAICompatInstrument.complete() sends in instruments.py, line ~288) is also handled by the server. I found both shapes referenced across docs/PRs but no single authoritative doc confirming both are accepted simultaneously today — **flag as version-dependent; verify empirically against the built stand-in / an actual llama-server before assuming Runesmith's nested-shape requests work.** Prior bugs on this exact path: issues #10732, #11847, #11988 (all closed, #11988 fixed by #12168).
- A separate `grammar` (raw GBNF) parameter also exists; sending both `grammar` and `response_format` together has been reported to error with "Either 'json_schema' or 'grammar' can be specified, but not both" (issue #11847) — send at most one.
- Malformed/unsupported schemas can make grammar conversion fail: reported causes include a schema property with only "description" and no "type" (#19716), a `pattern` regex missing `^`/`$` anchors ("Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'"), and `\/`-escaped regex in pattern (#27397, "400 Failed to initialize samplers: failed to parse grammar"). These are documented as HTTP 400 failures, but issue #19051 reports at least one class of grammar-parse failure that "fails open" (logs an error but proceeds to generate unconstrained text) rather than returning an HTTP error — so a stand-in should be able to simulate both a hard 400 and a silent-passthrough case.

KoboldCpp: added support for OpenAI-style Structured Outputs (`response_format` with `json_schema`), also accepts a JSON schema as a stringified value in its native `grammar` field, and converts JSON Schema → GBNF internally. I did not find a single authoritative KoboldCpp doc page with a worked request/response example (the wiki page I fetched came back truncated) — corroborated only via search-engine synthesis, so treat the exact request shape as needing empirical verification too.
specs.context_window:
llama-server: `--ctx-size` (alias `-c`, maps to n_ctx) — README states verbatim default is "0, 0 = loaded from model" (i.e., it inherits the context length baked into the GGUF's metadata unless you pass an explicit value). Some third-party sources describe a fallback built-in default around 2048–4096 tokens when a model lacks usable metadata; I could not confirm that exact fallback number in the primary README, so treat it as uncertain/version-dependent. `--ctx-size` is a shared budget across `--parallel` slots, not per-request (github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/11681) — with `--parallel N`, each slot effectively gets ctx-size/N. **Action-relevant for Runesmith**: your stated requests (9,000–15,000 prompt + 3,000–8,000 answer = ~12k–23k tokens) will overflow many GGUF models' native/default context, so any faithful stand-in (and any real llama-server the user points Runesmith at) needs an explicit `-c` of at least ~24000 to be safe, and Runesmith's own "llama.cpp server" preset blurb (providers.py PRESETS['llamacpp']) currently just says `llama-server -m model.gguf` with no `-c` flag.

KoboldCpp: `--contextsize N` sets context length; I found stale-looking wiki text claiming "16k for GGML, 32k for GGUF" (github.com/LostRuins/koboldcpp/wiki) that predates GGUF being the only real format in use today — do not trust that number, it reads as outdated documentation rather than a current limit.

runesmith_gaps: instruments.py lines 35-40: TRANSPORT_MARKERS/OUTPUT_MARKERS have no entry matching llama.cpp's context-overflow signature ("exceed_context_size_error" / "exceeds the available context size"). Because classify() (line 44-51) falls back to `return "transport"` for anything unmatched, a context-overflow 400 from llama-server gets treated as a transient transport failure: Router.call() (instruments.py lines 370-388) will retry it through the full DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S ladder (15,30,45,60,90,120,180s ≈ 9 minutes) before finally raising TransportCensored — even though the failure is deterministic and retrying can never succeed. Suggest adding a marker like "exceed_context_size_error" or "exceeds the available context size" to OUTPUT_MARKERS (or a new immediate-fail class) so it's charged as one call and reported in plain words ("prompt too long for this server's context window") instead of burning 9 minutes of retries.

instruments.py line 40: OUTPUT_MARKERS includes the literal substring "bad_request", but llama.cpp's actual malformed-schema/grammar failures use type "invalid_request_error" and messages like "failed to parse grammar" or "Pattern must start with '^' and end with '$'" — none contain "bad_request", so these also fall through classify()'s transport default and get needlessly retried, same as the context-overflow case above.

providers.py PRESETS['llamacpp'] (lines 27-29): blurb/setup only says “llama-server -m model.gguf” with no -c flag. Given --ctx-size's documented default is 0 (load from model metadata) and Runesmith's own stated prompts run 9,000-15,000 tokens plus 3,000-8,000 answer tokens, a user following this exact blurb on a model whose baked-in context is smaller than ~20-24k will hit the exceed_context_size_error above on the very first real call. Consider changing the setup hint to something like `llama-server -m model.gguf -c 24576` (or a similarly sized default) so out-of-the-box usage doesn't immediately fail for non-technical users.

providers.py discover_local() (line 86, timeout=0.8s default) and list_models() (line 103, timeout=8.0s default): both are far shorter than the cold-model-load time router mode can incur on first contact (huggingface.co's blog gives no hard number but frames it as potentially many seconds for a large GGUF). A router-mode llama-server that is up but hasn't loaded anything yet could time out on discovery/listing even though it would otherwise answer a real chat request within Runesmith's 600s OpenAICompatInstrument.timeout_s. Not a correctness bug (discovery is best-effort/advisory), but worth a UI caveat if you add router-mode support explicitly.

providers.py PRESETS has no KoboldCpp entry. Since KoboldCpp does expose an OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models (per your FAMILY note and the docs cited above), it could be added as a "kind": "openai" preset with base_url "http://127.0.0.1:5001/v1" alongside "llamacpp"/"lmstudio", and folded into discover_local()'s probe loop (line 93's tuple) — this is an addition opportunity, not a bug, and I have not verified KoboldCpp's /v1/models response shape matches the {"data":[{"id":...}]} format list_models() expects (see endpoints field), so that should be confirmed before wiring it in.

instruments.py OpenAICompatInstrument.complete() (line 284) never sends "stream": true and always parses a single choices[0].message.content — consistent with both servers' non-streaming behavior, so no gap there, but worth confirming a faithful stand-in defaults to non-streaming responses to match.

Endpoints include /v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/models (OpenAI-shaped), plus non-OpenAI extras. Auth: LOCALAI_API_KEY env var (comma-separated list for multiple keys) or LOCALAI_AUTH=true for full multi-user auth; accepted headers are `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, `x-api-key`, `xi-api-key`, or a `token` cookie; "if you configure neither authentication mode, the authentication middleware does not restrict requests" [https://localai.io/docs/features/authentication/]. /v1/models requires auth when auth is enabled (it is NOT in the public/unauthenticated route list).

JAN — Jan's own "Local API Server" (Settings → Local API Server) listens on 127.0.0.1:1337 by default (0.0.0.0 optional for LAN), API prefix /v1, layout deliberately mirrors api.openai.com/v1 [https://www.jan.ai/docs/desktop/api-server] [https://www.jan.ai/docs/desktop/api-preference]. Endpoints: GET /v1/models (OpenAI-shaped {"object":"list","data":[{"id":...,"object":"model"}]}), POST /v1/chat/completions (OpenAI-compatible, streaming/tools supported), plus a non-OpenAI POST /v1/messages (Anthropic-shaped, needs x-api-key not Bearer) and a stated-"coming soon" /v1/responses. Auth: any non-empty string works as the Bearer key ("set any string as your API key — it's only for local authentication"); leaving the key empty disables the auth check. Because Jan's engine is llama.cpp, its actual request/response wire behavior (response_format shape, context-limit error text, /v1/models fields) should be read off the llama.cpp server README directly: https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md — default port there is 8080 (Jan overrides this to 1337), --api-key supports a comma-separated key list, default `none`.

MSTY — low confidence / possibly not relevant. Msty bundles its own "Local AI Service"; one source cites port 10000 as its default, but this could not be corroborated from Msty's own docs, which describe only "Settings → Local AI Service → Service Endpoint → Network IP" without stating a fixed port, an OpenAI-endpoint-shape confirmation, or auth requirements [https://docs.msty.app/how-to-guides/make-local-ai-service-available-on-the-network]. Msty's own "Remote Model Providers → Msty Remote" networking path reads as a proprietary Msty-to-Msty protocol, not a generic third-party OpenAI-compatible surface — I could not confirm an external app like Runesmith can point at it the same way it points at vLLM/LocalAI/llama.cpp. Treat Msty as unverified; do not build a faithful stand-in from these notes alone.
specs.structured_output:
VLLM (current docs, "latest"): supported by default on /v1/chat/completions. Preferred path is `response_format: {"type": "json_schema", "json_schema": {"name": ..., "schema": {...}}}` (OpenAI-nested shape) — this is the SAME shape Runesmith already sends (runesmith/instruments.py:287-289). Plain `response_format: {"type": "json_object"}` is also still accepted (unconstrained-but-valid JSON) [https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/structured_outputs/]. Separately, vLLM had a `guided_json`/`guided_choice`/`guided_regex`/`guided_grammar` extra_body family; these were REMOVED as of v0.12.0 in favor of a single `structured_outputs` extra_body field (`{"structured_outputs": {"json": ...}}` etc.) [https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/structured_outputs/, search-corroborated]. Runesmith does not use guided_*/structured_outputs at all (it only ever sends `response_format`), so this migration doesn't hit Runesmith directly — but it shows vLLM's structured-output surface is not stable across versions. Known landmine (not applicable to Runesmith's code today, but worth knowing): on some vLLM builds between dev tags `0.23.1rc1...` and `0.26.1rc1...`, sending the legacy top-level `guided_json` silently returns HTTP 200 with unconstrained non-JSON text instead of erroring — fixed by PR #54285 [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/53975]. Default structured-output backend is "auto" (picks xgrammar/outlines/guidance based on the request); backend is configurable via --structured-outputs-config.backend.

LOCALAI: LocalAI's own documented mechanism is a bespoke top-level `grammar` field taking raw BNF, e.g. `{"model":"gpt-4","messages":[...],"grammar":"root ::= (\"yes\"|\"no\")"}`, explicitly stated to work "only ... for models that use the llama.cpp backend" [https://localai.io/docs/features/constrained_grammars/]. Separately (not fully doc-confirmed but corroborated by source-level search results), LocalAI also honors the OpenAI-standard `response_format: {"type":"json_object"}` by generating a BNF grammar internally "if supported" by the active backend — i.e., this works for llama.cpp-backed models but is NOT guaranteed across LocalAI's other backends (vLLM-backend, diffusers, transformers, exllama2, etc.). This is exactly the kind of backend-dependent behavior a strict client can trip on: Runesmith's default json_mode="json_object" should work against a llama.cpp-backed LocalAI model, but against a non-llama.cpp LocalAI backend the response_format may be silently ignored and the model may return prose, which Runesmith's tolerant_json fallback (instruments.py:92-112) is designed to catch — but only if the JSON happens to be embedded in the prose.

JAN / llama.cpp: llama.cpp's server (Jan's engine) supports `response_format` with BOTH plain `{"type":"json_object"}` and schema-constrained forms — but its schema-constrained shape is FLAT: `{"type":"json_schema","schema":{...}}`, NOT OpenAI/vLLM's nested `{"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":...,"schema":{...}}}` [https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md, fetched verbatim]. This is a real, version-independent structural mismatch versus vLLM/OpenAI. Runesmith always sends the NESTED shape (instruments.py:287-289: `body["response_format"] = {"type":"json_schema","json_schema":{"name":"answer","schema":schema}}`). Runesmith's default is json_mode="json_object" everywhere (OpenAICompatInstrument.__init__ default, instruments.py:271), so this mismatch is dormant today — but if json_mode is ever set to "json_schema" for the "llamacpp", "lmstudio" (also llama.cpp-based) or a future "jan" preset, the request would carry an extra unrecognized "json_schema" key llama.cpp doesn't expect, whose effect (ignored vs 400) I could not independently confirm and should be tested empirically against a real llama.cpp/Jan server.

MSTY: no structured-output documentation found; unverified.
specs.context_window:
None of these three families expose a single documented "default" context length the way a hosted API might — it's set per-model at launch time and enforced server-side, and prompts beyond it are REJECTED (400), not silently truncated (llama.cpp-family) or are config/backend dependent (LocalAI).

VLLM: set via --max-model-len; if omitted, "automatically derived from the model config" (max_position_embeddings / model_max_length in config.json). If the user-specified value exceeds what the model config supports, vLLM errors out at startup unless VLLM_ALLOW_LONG_MAX_MODEL_LEN=1 is set [search-derived, cross-checked against docs.vllm.ai engine_args + community reports]. At request time, exceeding the effective context returns an OpenAI-style message: "This model's maximum context length is X tokens. However, you requested Y tokens (Z in the messages, W in the completion). Please reduce the length of the messages or completion." as a 400 [https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/20409, historically identical OpenAI wording — vLLM deliberately mirrors it].

LOCALAI (llama.cpp backend): context_size is set in the model's YAML config (`context_size: N`), and changing it requires a container/server restart [https://github.com/mudler/LocalAI/issues/8647]. Exceeding it returns: "request (X tokens) exceeds the available context size (Y tokens), try increasing it" — corroborated as a 400 in adjacent llama.cpp/continue.dev reports, but I could not pin the exact status code from LocalAI's own docs directly, only from llama.cpp-adjacent issue trackers — treat the status code as "very likely 400, not independently confirmed on LocalAI's docs site."

JAN / llama.cpp directly (most reliable citation, from the llama.cpp server README + issue trackers): --ctx-size sets it (no fixed universal default stated in the README excerpt fetched); exceeding it returns HTTP 400 with message "the request exceeds the available context size. try increasing the context size or enable context shift" [https://github.com/continuedev/continue/issues/9797, https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/57166, cross-corroborated across three independent client-integration bug reports]. This is the single most load-bearing, well-corroborated error string in this whole spec, since Runesmith's 9,000-15,000-token prompts are exactly the shape that will trip small-context local models.

MSTY: unverified, no data found.

runesmith_gaps: runesmith/instruments.py:35-51 (TRANSPORT_MARKERS/OUTPUT_MARKERS/classify): none of the context-length-exceeded error strings documented above ('This model's maximum context length is...', 'the request exceeds the available context size...', 'exceeds the available context size') contain any TRANSPORT_MARKERS or OUTPUT_MARKERS substring, and classify()'s explicit fallback is 'unknown errors are transport' (line 45-51). Today it will be retried through the FULL DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S ladder (15+30+45+60+90+120+180 = 540s) before TransportCensored is raised — wasting ~9 minutes per call on a deterministic, non-transient failure that will fail identically on every retry, and then getting reported as a censored opportunity rather than a clear 'your prompt is too big for this model' message to a non-technical user.

specs.install_and_start:
All seven are hosted APIs except LiteLLM Proxy (self-hosted) and Clive (a local CLI, N/A per above). None require anything to be "installed" for Runesmith's purposes beyond obtaining a key — Runesmith just needs base_url + key.

OpenRouter: sign up at openrouter.ai (no card needed for the ":free" models), create a key at https://openrouter.ai/keys. Matches Runesmith's existing preset (runesmith/app/providers.py:30-33).

Groq: sign up at console.groq.com, create a key at https://console.groq.com/keys. Matches existing preset (:34-37) — but see gaps below, its suggested model list is stale.

Google AI Studio / Gemini: sign in with a Google account at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey, click "Create API key" — no card required for Flash/Flash-Lite. Matches existing preset (:38-41).

Mistral: sign up at console.mistral.ai, create a key at https://console.mistral.ai/api-keys; the account starts in "Free mode" automatically (docs.mistral.ai/admin/user-management-finops/tier). Matches existing preset (:42-44).

GitHub Models: DEAD. GitHub's own changelog says it "is now retired" as of 2026-07-30 — playground, model catalog, inference API and bring-your-own-key are "no longer available to any customer, including existing customers" (github.blog/changelog/2026-07-30-github-models-is-now-retired/). New customers were already locked out from 2026-06-16 (github.blog/changelog/2026-06-16-github-models-is-no-longer-available-to-new-customers/). Do not build a preset for this; GitHub's own migration guidance points to Azure AI Foundry or GitHub Copilot instead (docs.github.com/en/github-models/prototyping-with-ai-models), neither of which is a comparable free OpenAI-compatible chat endpoint.

Cloudflare Workers AI: sign up for a free Cloudflare account at dash.cloudflare.com, note your Account ID, create an API token with Workers AI permissions. The 10,000 free Neurons/day apply "whether on the Free or Paid Workers plan" (developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/) — no separate paid Workers plan is required just to get the daily allocation. No preset exists in Runesmith today.

LiteLLM Proxy (self-hosted "custom gate," cross-platform Windows/macOS/Linux, needs Python 3.10+): `uv tool install 'litellm[proxy]'` (or `pip install 'litellm[proxy]'`), write a config.yaml naming a model plus its own api_base/api_key (pointing at, e.g., Groq or OpenRouter), then run `litellm --config your_config.yaml`. It listens on **port 4000** by default (http://0.0.0.0:4000) (docs.litellm.ai/docs/proxy/quick_start). A Runesmith user would enter base_url http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1 under the existing "custom" preset (runesmith/app/providers.py:58-60) — no new preset id is needed, just documentation. It is not itself a free-model source; whatever quota limits apply below (Groq's 8K TPM, etc.) still apply to whatever you put behind it, unless you also set a stricter rpm/tpm on the LiteLLM virtual key.

specs.context_window:
Answering directly: for each provider, would a Runesmith request (9,000-15,000 prompt tokens + 3,000-8,000 requested max_tokens, i.e. roughly 12,000-23,000 tokens "spent" against any budget that counts both) blow a free-tier per-minute/per-day ceiling?

OpenRouter (free ":free" models): no documented per-minute TOKEN ceiling at all — the free-tier limit is pure request-count: 20 requests/minute always, and 50 requests/day (accounts with <$10 lifetime credit) or 1,000 requests/day (accounts with ≥$10 lifetime credit) (openrouter.ai/docs/api-reference/limits). A single 10-15k token call is not itself rejected for size by OpenRouter's own layer — but the underlying free model behind it may have its own context window and may reject or truncate.

Groq (free tier, current lineup openai/gpt-oss-20b, openai/gpt-oss-120b, openai/gpt-oss-safeguard-20b, qwen/qwen3.8-27b): **8,000 tokens/minute (TPM)**, charged against prompt tokens + your *declared* max_tokens, not what the model actually emits (console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits; corroborated by openclaw/openclaw#147644 and inferenceapis.com/reference/errors/groq-413-request-too-large). This is smaller than the smallest Runesmith request by itself (a 9,000-token prompt alone already exceeds 8,000). A Runesmith call at default sizing against these Groq free models will reliably 413, every time, regardless of retries. (The now-deprecated llama-3.3-70b-versatile had a looser 12,000 TPM/1,000 RPD before its 2026-08-16 shutdown, per the same rate-limits doc history — still short of 15k+8k, but closer.)

Google AI Studio / Gemini: TPM is generous — 1,000,000 TPM has historically been cited for Flash (multiple secondary 2026 sources; Google's own rate-limits page no longer publishes exact free-tier numbers and instead says "view your active rate limits in AI Studio," ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/rate-limits). The binding free-tier constraint is **RPM**, cited around 10-15 RPM for Flash / Flash-Lite (5 RPM historically for Pro before Pro left the free tier — see below) and **RPD** (roughly 250/day for Flash, 1,000/day for Flash-Lite per secondary sources). A single 10-15k token request comfortably fits the TPM budget; you're limited to a handful of calls per minute, not by size.

Mistral: free/"Experiment" tier numeric limits are **no longer published**; Mistral's own docs say "check Admin Console → Limits" (docs.mistral.ai/admin/user-management-finops/tier, help.mistral.ai/en/articles/698531). Older/secondary figures cite roughly 1 request/second and up to ~500,000 TPM historically, plus an overall ~1 billion tokens/month cap — if still accurate, a single 10-15k token call is nowhere near the TPM ceiling; the 1 req/sec cap is the practical throttle for back-to-back calls, not size.

GitHub Models: N/A, retired 2026-07-30.

Cloudflare Workers AI: no TPM/RPM as such — the free budget is **10,000 "Neurons"/day, shared across all models**, resetting at 00:00 UTC (developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/platform/pricing/). Using the documented per-model Neuron rates: @cf/openai/gpt-oss-20b costs 18,182 neurons/M input tokens + 27,273 neurons/M output tokens, so a 12,000-prompt + 5,000-output Runesmith call costs roughly 12,000×0.018182 + 5,000×0.027273 ≈ 218 + 136 ≈ **355 neurons**, i.e. about **28 such calls per day** before the daily allocation is exhausted. Llama-3.1-8b is worse: 25,608/75,147 per M in/out → roughly 307+376 ≈ **683 neurons/call**, about **14 calls/day**. This is a daily ceiling, not a per-minute one, but it will exhaust fast in any multi-loop Runesmith batch run.

LiteLLM Proxy: no limit of its own unless you configure rpm/tpm on a virtual key; otherwise it simply forwards to whichever of the above sits behind it, and that provider's ceiling (most notably Groq's 8,000 TPM) still applies.

Every Runesmith call against Groq's free tier at default sizing will 413, deterministically, not intermittently. runesmith/instruments.py's TRANSPORT_MARKERS (lines 35-39) list "429" and "rate_limited" as transport markers but not "413" or Groq's actual body strings ("rate_limit_exceeded", "tokens per minute"); classify() (lines 44-51) still defaults unmatched messages to "transport" so retries will still fire, but they're pointless here since backoff cannot fix a fixed size-vs-budget mismatch — worth a special case (e.g. detect HTTP 413 and either fail fast with a plain-words explanation, or auto-shrink max_tokens once and retry) rather than spending the full 7-attempt backoff ladder (DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S, line 41) on something retrying can't solve.

runesmith/app/providers.py:38-41 (Gemini preset): suggested model "gemini-2.5-pro" has disputed free-tier status as of 2026-09-28. Google's own pricing page (ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing) still marks its Free Tier column "Free of charge" when fetched today, but multiple independent 2026 secondary sources report Pro-series models (2.5 Pro, 3.x Pro) were pulled from the AI Studio free tier around 2026-04-01 and now require a paid Vertex AI project. GitHub Models, one of the seven families asked about, is fully retired (2026-07-30, per GitHub's own changelog). No preset should be built for it; if one ever existed in planning notes it should be removed.

Cloudflare Workers AI has no preset in runesmith/app/providers.py today. If added: (a) its base_url is not a flat constant like every existing preset — it embeds an account_id in the path (https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/{account_id}/ai/v1) — PRESETS' current dict shape (base_url as a plain string, id/label/base_url/key/key_url/suggested/blurb) has no templating slot for that, so either the base_url field needs a `{account_id}` placeholder convention or the setup blurb needs to tell the user to paste their account ID into the URL by hand; (b) the free daily budget (10,000 Neurons, shared across all models) supports roughly 14-28 Runesmith-sized calls per day depending on model (see context_window field for the arithmetic) — far too little for a multi-loop batch run; the blurb should say this plainly rather than just "free tier" the way other presets do.

Mistral preset (runesmith/app/providers.py:42-44) and Mistral's free-tier claim are structurally fine, but avoid hard-coding remembered numeric limits (e.g. "1 req/sec, 500K TPM") into user-facing text — Mistral's own docs say these are no longer published and vary per workspace (docs.mistral.ai/admin/user-management-finops/tier); if Runesmith ever surfaces a rate-limit explanation to the user for Mistral, point them to admin.mistral.ai/plateforme/limits rather than asserting a number.

LiteLLM Proxy fits Runesmith's existing "custom" preset (runesmith/app/providers.py:58-60) as-is — base_url http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1, any string as the key unless a master/virtual key is configured — no new preset id is needed, only a how-to note. Its own default port (4000) is not in discover_local()'s probe list (runesmith/app/providers.py:86-99, which only checks Ollama :11434, LM Studio :1234, llama.cpp :8080); adding a GET /models probe against 127.0.0.1:4000 would let discover_local() find a locally-running LiteLLM proxy the same way it finds the other three local servers, for users who self-host it as their 'custom gate.'

OpenRouter's response_format support is per-model and silently ignored when unsupported (openrouter.ai's own structured-outputs guide). Runesmith's tolerant_json=True default (runesmith/instruments.py:274, used in parse_json_answer at :92-112) helps by scanning prose for an embedded JSON object, but there's no verification that a free OpenRouter model actually followed the requested schema's required fields — worth a note in Runesmith's own docs that OpenRouter free-model JSON compliance is best-effort, not guaranteed, same as any other provider where response_format isn't honoured.

specs.family: Cline CLI — npm package `cline` (Cline Bot Inc.), Apache-2.0, open source (github.com/cline/cline, apps/cli). It shares its agent core with the Cline VS Code/JetBrains extensions and the Cline SDK. IMPORTANT distinction found while researching: "Cline CLI" (a terminal agent you run as a subprocess) and the separate "Cline API" (a hosted OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint at api.cline.bot) are two different products with different rules — see `endpoints` and `runesmith_gaps` below. Neither is the same thing as an OpenAI-compatible model server Runesmith could point `OpenAICompatInstrument` at out of the box.

specs.endpoints:
Two separate things, do not conflate them:

(1) Cline CLI non-interactive/one-shot mode (no HTTP server of its own): `npm i -g cline`, then `cline "<prompt>"` runs one turn and exits; `cline` alone opens the interactive TUI; `cline --kanban` opens the kanban board. Headless behavior triggers automatically on `--json`, piped stdin, or redirected stdout (docs.cline.bot/usage/cli-overview). Key flags for driving it from another program: `--json` (NDJSON to stdout instead of styled text), `-y/--yolo` (skip all tool-approval prompts, full autonomy, "everything streams to stdout"), `--auto-approve <bool>` (default true), `-m/--model <id>`, `-P/--provider <id>` (default `cline`), `-k/--key <api-key>` (override key for this run), `--thinking <none|low|medium|high|xhigh>`, `--retries <count>` (default 3, max consecutive mistakes before halting), `-t/--timeout <seconds>` (0 = no limit), `-c/--cwd <path>`, `--config <path>` (default `~/.cline/data/settings`), `--data-dir <path>` (isolated state), `-s/--system <prompt>` (replace system instructions), `--id <session-id>` (resume), `-z/--zen` (fire to background hub daemon and exit immediately), `--acp` (Agent Client Protocol, JSON-RPC-over-stdio for editor integration — still not HTTP), `-v/--verbose`, `-V/--version`, `-h/--help`. Subcommands: `auth`, `config`, `connect` (chat-platform connectors), `mcp`, `dev`, `doctor`, `history`, `hook`, `plugin`, `schedule`, `hub`, `update`, `version`, `kanban`. Sources: docs.cline.bot/cli/cli-reference, docs.cline.bot/usage/cli-overview, github.com/cline/cline/blob/main/apps/cli/README.md (fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com), cline.bot/cli, cline.ghost.io/introducing-cline-cli-2-0.

(2) Cline API (a genuinely OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint, separate product): `POST https://api.cline.bot/api/v1/chat/completions`, or point an OpenAI SDK at `base_url="https://api.cline.bot/api/v1"`. Auth: `Authorization: Bearer $CLINE_API_KEY`, key created at app.cline.bot under Settings > API Keys. Documented body fields: `model` (e.g. `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"`), `messages`, `stream`. A `GET /models`-style listing endpoint was not found in the docs pages I could fetch (docs.cline.bot/api/overview, docs.cline.bot/api/sdk-examples) — treat as unconfirmed, not "absent." Source: docs.cline.bot/api/overview, docs.cline.bot/api/sdk-examples.
specs.structured_output:
Two different meanings again:

CLI `--json` mode is an event stream of the agent's own reasoning/tool-call/message activity, not a single schema-conformant JSON answer: one JSON object per line (NDJSON), fields `type` ("ask" or "say"), `text`, `ts` (unix ms), a `say`/`ask` subtype (e.g. `"say":"text"`), optional `reasoning`, and `partial` (bool, true while a message is still streaming). Example line from docs: `{"type":"say","text":"I'll create the file now.","ts":1760501486669,"say":"text"}`. Consumers are expected to pipe/filter it, e.g. `cline --json "List all TODO comments" | jq -r 'select(.type=="agent_event" and .event.text) | .event.text'`. There is no documented flag to force the CLI to emit one final JSON object matching a caller-supplied JSON Schema the way Runesmith's `response_format: json_schema`/`json_object` does — Runesmith would have to parse the NDJSON stream itself and extract the final answer text, then run its own `parse_json_answer`. Sources: docs.cline.bot/cli/cli-reference, cline.bot/cli.

Cline API (api.cline.bot): described only as "OpenAI-compatible"; the specific pages I could fetch (docs.cline.bot/api/overview, docs.cline.bot/api/sdk-examples) did not state whether `response_format: json_object` / `json_schema` is honored — this is UNCONFIRMED, not verified either way, and should be tested rather than assumed before Runesmith relies on it.
specs.context_window: Not a fixed Cline-CLI property. Both the CLI and the Cline API are pass-throughs to whichever underlying model is selected (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, OpenRouter, AWS Bedrock, GCP Vertex, Cerebras, Groq, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including local Ollama/LM Studio) — context window is whatever that model provides (docs.cline.bot/usage/cli-overview; docs.cline.bot/provider-config/openai-compatible). Nothing in the pages I fetched documents a Cline-imposed ceiling on prompt size, and I found no statement about how the CLI or API behaves with a 9,000–15,000-token prompt plus a 3,000–8,000-token answer (Runesmith's actual request size) — this is UNCONFIRMED and should be tested against the real service rather than assumed.

runesmith_gaps: runesmith/instruments.py OpenAICompatInstrument does `POST {base}/chat/completions` over HTTP. The Cline CLI does not run an HTTP server at all — its non-interactive interface is a subprocess you invoke per call (`cline --json "prompt"`) that streams NDJSON events to stdout, so OpenAICompatInstrument cannot be pointed at 'Cline CLI' the way it is pointed at Ollama/LM Studio/llama.cpp. Driving it would need a new subprocess-based Instrument kind that spawns the process, feeds the prompt, reads the NDJSON stream, and extracts the final say/text event as the 'answer' — a materially different transport than anything currently in instruments.py.

runesmith/app/providers.py discover_local() only probes fixed local ports/paths: GET http://127.0.0.1:11434/api/tags (Ollama) and GET {base}/models on 127.0.0.1:1234 (LM Studio) and 127.0.0.1:8080 (llama.cpp). Cline CLI does not listen on any local port in its documented one-shot/--json/--yolo modes, so it will never be discovered this way even when installed.

The separate api.cline.bot REST endpoint IS a real POST {base}/chat/completions server and could in principle be added as a PRESETS entry like openrouter/groq — but per docs.cline.bot/getting-started/free-models, free-model usage is explicitly NOT available through that API (only through the IDE extension and CLI's own login-gated provider), so a preset pointed at api.cline.bot would never surface a 'free' model the way the existing openrouter/groq presets' 'suggested' free models do — it contradicts the premise of this research request (looking for free models Runesmith's non-technical users can reach without a paid key).

Cline's free-model promotions are both account-gated (require signing into a 'Cline account' via `cline auth`, an interactive/OAuth flow) and time-limited/rotating (e.g. Grok Code Fast free at CLI-2.0 launch per cline.ghost.io; Minimax M2.5 and Kimi K2.5 free 'for a limited time' per the same 2.0 announcement, both superseded by whatever is current as of 2026-09). runesmith/instruments.py secret_from() only reads a plain env var or a key=value line from a .env file — it has no mechanism for an interactive OAuth login, so even a hypothetical subprocess Instrument could not unattended-authenticate to reach Cline's free tier the way it authenticates to OpenRouter/Groq with a static bearer key.

None of this is a small local model Runesmith could run offline the way Ollama/LM Studio presets do; it is entirely a hosted, account-gated, rotating promotion on Cline's own infrastructure.

synthesis.cline_verdict:
No — not as a source of free inference the way Runesmith uses "free models" today, for two independent, verified reasons, plus the user's own wording is itself ambiguous and should be confirmed.

1. Ambiguous target. The user wrote "Clive" (spelled with an i). Two distinct real tools match: (a) SedarOlmez94/clive (github.com/SedarOlmez94/clive, dev.to/sedarolmez94/..., Rust, v0.1.0, last visible activity Aug 2024) — a thin terminal chat client that wraps a local Ollama server; it has no HTTP server or model catalog of its own, so it adds nothing Runesmith's existing "ollama" preset (runesmith/app/providers.py:19-23) doesn't already reach directly at http://127.0.0.1:11434. (b) Cline (docs.cline.bot, no "i") — a real, actively developed coding-agent CLI/IDE extension (apps/cli, npm package `cline`) that does currently promote rotating free models. If the user meant (a), the answer is simply "no new capability, already covered." The rest of this verdict addresses (b), the substantive case.

2. Architecture mismatch. Runesmith's OpenAICompatInstrument (runesmith/instruments.py:264-321) only knows how to POST JSON to `{base_url}/chat/completions` and parse a `choices[0].message.content` string. Cline CLI's non-interactive/one-shot mode (`cline --json "<prompt>"`) is not an HTTP server at all — it is a subprocess that streams NDJSON "say"/"ask" events to stdout (docs.cline.bot/cli/cli-reference). Pointing Runesmith at it would require an entirely new subprocess-based Instrument kind (spawn, feed prompt, read NDJSON, extract the final text event, run it through Runesmith's own parse_json_answer), not a `base_url` in the existing PRESETS list.

3. Policy wall, confirmed from Cline's own docs. Cline's separate, genuinely OpenAI-compatible REST endpoint (`https://api.cline.bot/api/v1/chat/completions`) is the one shape that *would* fit OpenAICompatInstrument unmodified — but docs.cline.bot/getting-started/free-models states explicitly that free-model usage is available only through the Cline IDE Extension and the CLI's own `cline`/`ClinePass` provider, and is NOT available through the api.cline.bot REST API. So the one interface shaped like what Runesmith needs is precisely the one Cline excludes free models from.

4. Auth mismatch. Even setting up the subprocess path, Cline's free tier requires an interactive `cline auth` login to a Cline account (OAuth-flavored), which is account-gated and time-limited/rotating (whatever model is free today — Grok Code Fast, Minimax M2.5, Kimi K2.5 — is explicitly stated to change). Runesmith's `secret_from()` (runesmith/instruments.py:136-146) only reads a static env var or `.env` line; it has no mechanism to drive an interactive login, so even a hypothetical subprocess Instrument could not authenticate unattended.

Net: do not build a Cline preset or Instrument kind for this purpose. It would take real new code (a subprocess transport) to reach a free-model surface that Cline's own docs say isn't exposed through the interface that subprocess would use anyway. Ollama (already supported), OpenRouter's ":free" models, Groq's free tier (mind the 8,000 TPM ceiling), and Google AI Studio's Gemini Flash/Flash-Lite remain the legitimate free paths already reachable through Runesmith's existing OpenAI-compatible presets. If Lars specifically wants Cline integrated as a component later, flag it as a distinct feature request (new subprocess Instrument + one-time human login step), not a "free model" fix.
conformance_requirements: 1. Before sending any request to a local-preset instrument (ollama, lmstudio, llamacpp) whose context length is unconfirmed, Runesmith must estimate prompt+schema+max_tokens size and warn in plain language when it plausibly exceeds that preset's documented default context (Ollama 4,096, LM Studio 8,000, llama.cpp server 0=inherit-from-model) rather than sending blind — Runesmith's own prompts (9,000-15,000 in, 3,000-8,000 out) exceed all three defaults on every call.

2. classify() (runesmith/instruments.py:44-51) must not default HTTP 404 'model ... not found, try pulling it first' (Ollama) to error_kind='transport' — it is a permanent configuration error, not a transient one, and must resolve in one call, not the full ~540s DEFAULT_BACKOFF_S ladder.

3. classify() must not default HTTP 413 'tokens per minute' / 'rate_limit_exceeded' size-not-rate errors (Groq free tier, 8,000 TPM) to 'transport' — retrying cannot fix a fixed prompt-size-vs-budget mismatch; it must fail fast with a plain explanation.

4. classify() must not default HTTP 400 context-overflow bodies ('the request exceeds the available context size', 'maximum context length is X tokens', 'exceed_context_size_error' — llama.cpp/vLLM/LocalAI family) to 'transport' — this is deterministic and identical on every retry.
5. classify() must not default HTTP 400 response_format rejections ('response_format.type must be json_schema or text' — LM Studio) to 'transport' — retrying with the same body cannot succeed.

6. Any OpenAICompatInstrument built against the lmstudio preset must never send response_format:{'type':'json_object'} — LM Studio rejects it with HTTP 400 on every call per multiple corroborating bug reports; the effective json_mode for that preset must be 'json_schema' (with schema) or omit response_format (no schema), never 'json_object'.

7. The Studio UI (app/static/js/views/inference.js) must not unconditionally overwrite spec.json_mode='json_object' for every kind==='openai' provider on save — doing so guarantees requirement 6 can never hold in practice even if the backend default is fixed.

8. Before defaulting json_mode='json_schema' for any llama.cpp-family preset (llamacpp, lmstudio, a future jan), Runesmith must have empirically confirmed against a real or faithful stand-in server whether the OpenAI-nested response_format shape it always sends ({'type':'json_schema','json_schema':{'name':...,'schema':...}}) is honored, since llama.cpp's own README documents a flat shape ({'type':'json_schema','schema':...}) and simultaneous support for both is version-dependent and not settled by docs alone.

9. Provider setup text (providers.py PRESETS blurb/setup fields for ollama, lmstudio, llamacpp) must tell a non-technical owner how to raise context length before real use, since none of it is settable through the /v1/chat/completions endpoint Runesmith actually calls.

10. discover_local() must distinguish 'nothing is listening on 127.0.0.1:11434' (Ollama tray app closed/never launched — a normal Windows state, not an error) from other connection failures, and surface plain language pointing at the tray icon / Start menu / `ollama serve`.

11. Before calling Groq's free-tier models, Runesmith must check (or let the user check) that prompt_tokens + declared max_tokens stays under 8,000 — otherwise every call 413s deterministically at Runesmith's stated default sizing; this should be caught client-side, not discovered via a wasted retry ladder.

12. Presets/suggested-model lists must not name models that are dead or in disputed free-tier status without a caveat: Groq's llama-3.3-70b-versatile (shut down 2026-08-16) must be dropped; gemini-2.5-pro's free-tier status (disputed as of 2026-09-28) must be flagged or the suggested list narrowed to flash/flash-lite.

13. No preset, Instrument kind, or discovery probe should be added for GitHub Models (retired 2026-07-30, dead), Cline's api.cline.bot endpoint (free models explicitly excluded from it per Cline's own docs), or 'Clive' CLI (no HTTP surface, rides entirely on the existing Ollama preset).

14. Any new local-server preset (Jan :1337, KoboldCpp :5001, LiteLLM proxy :4000) must have its GET /v1/models response shape empirically confirmed to match the {'data':[{'id':...}]} convention list_models()/discover_local() assume before being wired in — this is unverified today for Jan and KoboldCpp.

A manual/CHANGELOG note (not a code fix) must state plainly that Ollama's context overflow is invisible to Runesmith: the server returns a normal HTTP 200 while silently dropping the front of the prompt (including system instructions/schema) to fit its context window, so a confusing or schema-failing answer with no error at all is an expected local-model failure mode, not a Runesmith bug.
