synthesis.manual_chapter_outline:
"Free thinking power" — chapter outline for the Runesmith manual, aimed at a non-technical owner. All facts below were checked against official docs/changelogs on 2026-09-27/28 (dates noted per section so the chapter can flag when to re-verify); every claim should carry its source URL as a footnote in the final chapter, not just this outline.

1. Why this chapter exists
   One paragraph: Runesmith needs something to answer its questions (an "instrument"); several good options cost nothing. This chapter is the map, roughly ordered from easiest to most advanced.

2. The easiest free path: Ollama, on your own computer (checked 2026-09-27 against docs.ollama.com)
   - Download from ollama.com/download, install, no admin rights needed on Windows.
   - Pull one model: `ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b` (Runesmith's own suggested starting model).
   - The gotcha to warn about up front, in plain words: on Windows, Ollama is a small icon that lives in your system tray, not a background service — if you quit it, or it never started, Runesmith will say it can't connect. Look for the llama icon, or reopen "Ollama" from the Start menu.
   - The second gotcha, equally important: Ollama's out-of-the-box "memory" for a conversation (its context window) defaults to about 4,096 tokens (docs.ollama.com/faq) — smaller than a single Runesmith request. Explain in one sentence, with a copy-pasteable fix: set the OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH environment variable (e.g. to 32000) before starting Ollama, or ask Runesmith's own setup step to do it. Say plainly what happens if this is skipped: not an error message — the model just seems to ignore instructions or give a confused answer, because the start of the request was quietly dropped.

3. A friendlier alternative: LM Studio (checked 2026-09-27 against lmstudio.ai/docs, app v0.4.25)
   - Download from lmstudio.ai/download, open the app, use the "Discover" tab to get a model.
   - The gotcha: the local server does NOT start automatically — you must open the Developer tab and switch "Start Server" on (or run `lms server start`).
   - The context-length gotcha: default is 8,000 tokens (raised from a smaller number in a June 2026 update) — still likely too small for Runesmith's real requests. Fix: My Models tab -> gear icon next to the model -> raise Context Length (try 16,384 or 32,768).
   - A LM-Studio-specific quirk worth mentioning if it's still true when this ships: it can reject a certain "loose JSON" request mode outright; if Runesmith reports an immediate failure the first time you test the connection, this is usually why, and the fix is on Runesmith's side (choosing the right JSON mode for LM Studio), not something to troubleshoot yourself.

4. For the technically curious: llama.cpp server (checked 2026-09-27 against github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp)
   - One line: this is the "bare metal" option, a single program you run from a terminal (`llama-server -m model.gguf -c 24576`), no app around it. Mention it exists; don't over-explain — this reader profile is not the target audience for it.

5. Free, hosted options — no download, just a free account and a key
   - OpenRouter (openrouter.ai): sign up, no card needed, create a key, pick any model ending in ":free". Limits: 20 requests/minute, 50/day (or 1,000/day once you've ever added $10 of credit, even unspent).
   - Groq (console.groq.com): very fast, free tier — but explain plainly that a single Runesmith request may simply be too big for Groq's free allowance (8,000 tokens/minute) and that this isn't a bug to chase, it's a size mismatch; suggest Groq for smaller/faster jobs, not the biggest Runesmith requests.
   - Google AI Studio / Gemini (aistudio.google.com/apikey): sign in with a Google account, create a key, no card. Recommend Flash or Flash-Lite specifically (Pro's free status was uncertain as of the date this was checked — verify before recommending it).
   - Mistral (console.mistral.ai): free "Experiment" tier automatically applied to a new account; exact limits are only visible in your own account console now, so don't quote a number, just point there.

6. What "free" doesn't mean
   One short section translating the shape of failure for each option above into plain words: a wait-and-retry message ("you're calling faster than allowed") versus a this-request-is-too-big message ("shrink what you're asking, don't just retry") versus a today's-allowance-is-gone message ("comes back at midnight UTC"). The goal: an owner who sees a failure recognizes which of these three buckets it's in without needing to read an error code.

7. A dead end to skip
   GitHub Models: retired by GitHub on 2026-07-30, permanently, for everyone. If you find an older guide mentioning it, skip it.

8. Two things that sound like model sources but aren't
   - "Clive" / "Cline" CLIs: both are chat/coding assistants you'd run in a terminal, not something Runesmith can plug into directly — Clive just talks to your own Ollama models (already covered in section 2); Cline has its own free-model promotions but only inside its own login-gated app, not through a connection Runesmith can use. If you've heard about either, this explains why Runesmith doesn't have a "Cline" option in its provider list.

9. Recap table (to close the chapter)
   Columns: Provider | Needs a key? | Where to start it | Practical context/size limit | One-line gotcha | Date these facts were checked. Populate from sections 2-5 above.
uncertain: Whether Ollama's /v1/chat/completions honors response_format.json_schema (schema-constrained) on the specific Ollama build a given user has installed — GitHub issue #10001 about this being ignored is closed but no fixed-in version was confirmed from docs alone; must be checked against `ollama --version` empirically, not assumed.

Whether Ollama's real current default context window is a flat 4,096 (docs.ollama.com/faq) or VRAM-scaled per docs.ollama.com/context-length — the two official pages disagree as of the research date; for the 'modest machine' audience both converge on ~4,096, but the discrepancy itself should be watched for a docs reconciliation.
LM Studio's exact enforcement of the json_schema.strict field — the docs show it as the string "true" rather than a JSON boolean; not confirmed which type LM Studio actually accepts/requires.

Whether llama.cpp server (and therefore Jan, which uses the same engine) accepts BOTH the flat {'type':'json_schema','schema':{...}} shape its README shows AND the OpenAI-nested {'json_schema':{'name':...,'schema':...}} shape Runesmith always sends — referenced across multiple PRs/issues but not confirmed as simultaneously-supported by a single authoritative source; needs an empirical test against the stand-in and then a real server.

KoboldCpp's GET /v1/models response shape — not independently confirmed to match the {'data':[{'id':...}]} convention that Runesmith's list_models()/discover_local() assume for any 'openai'-kind preset.

LM Studio's exact HTTP status for 'model id not downloaded' (404, community-reported, not in official docs) and for 'model mid-JIT-load' (503, community-reported) — lower confidence than the response_format/context findings.

llama.cpp router mode's separate non-/v1 GET /models endpoint's exact JSON shape (status field per model) — not independently confirmed; irrelevant to Runesmith today since it only calls /v1/models, but relevant if router mode is ever specifically supported.

The exact fallback context length llama-server uses when a GGUF's metadata lacks a usable value — some third-party sources cite ~2,048-4,096 tokens, not confirmed in the primary README, which just says the default is '0, 0 = loaded from model'.

Gemini's exact free-tier RPM/RPD numbers — Google's own rate-limits page no longer publishes them ('view your active rate limits in AI Studio'); figures used here came from secondary 2026 sources.
